title: Lira's Dragon Surprise
markdown:
The Ferncrown festival ribbons were woven from threads spun of the softest moonlight, adorned with tiny sparkling dewdrop pearls. Each was a miniature work of art, awarded to the most dazzling creations. Lira, a young elf with hair like spun moonlight and eyes as bright as a starling’s, longed to win one this year more than anything. Her little workshop in the quiet hidden terraces buzzed with the project.

Crafting a prize-winning decoration was no simple thing. A tiny flutter in her chest, like a trapped moth: fingers not nimble enough, stitches not neat, petals not perfectly placed. She practised intricate knots, brow furrowed. They always seemed a little uneven. A little off.

One sunny afternoon her neighbour Grumble the goblin shuffled over: lopsided grin, pockets bulging with a smooth stone, a shiny button, a stray acorn. Voice like pebbles downhill. “What’s that frown for, Lira?”

She showed him a small arrangement of dried flowers that, to her eyes, was decidedly wobbly. “It’s just not quite right. The festival is tomorrow. I don’t think my ribbon will be good enough. It won’t shine like the others.”

Grumble peered, stroked his chin. “Nonsense. You just need the freshest Moonpetal flowers, kissed by morning dew, for the best sparkle. And the most perfect dewdrop pearls. Let’s go to Whispering Woods. I’ll help you.”

His sturdy boots crunched. Her light steps barely disturbed a leaf. Cool air: damp earth, ancient pine, sweet unseen blossoms. Secrets on the breeze. Lira stopped. Breath catching.

“Look.” Pressed deep in emerald moss: a footprint. Enormous, far larger than Grumble’s entire foot, three long curious toes. Another, and another, breadcrumbs into the shadowy woods. The air grew still. Their own steps seemed impossibly loud.

“Who might have made those?” Grumble’s eyes wide.

“Perhaps a creature much too big for our quiet little festival. Perhaps something unexpected.”

They followed, hearts like tiny drums. The tracks led to a sun-dappled clearing. Among giant feathery ferns sat a colossal creature, scales the muted greens and browns of ancient moss, gentle puffs of smoke—not fierce fire—sighing from its nostrils. A dragon. It did not roar. A low rumble like distant summer thunder, enormous bewildered golden eyes, fumbling clumsily with a large ornate set of spectacles perched precariously on its snout.

“Oh, botheration,” the dragon rumbled, warm honey. “Where have my spectacles gone? I can’t see a single dewdrop sparkle without them.”

Lira and Grumble exchanged glances. Not a fearsome beast of legend. A rather lost and slightly grumbling dragon.

“Excuse me,” Lira said, voice trembling a little, firm with kindness. “Did you lose something, sir?”

A small puff of surprise. “Goodness me! You startled me, little ones. Yes, my spectacles. I’m Puff. I can barely see my own snout without them.”

“We’re Lira and Grumble. We’re looking for Moonpetal flowers for the festival ribbon. Maybe your spectacles fell nearby while you were searching?”

Puff’s mossy head bobbed like a friendly buoy. “They fell off when I was admiring the—I’m not quite sure what. Everything was a bit blurry.”

They searched ferns and fallen leaves. Puff’s rumble grew louder, frustration making nearby leaves tremble. Lira and Grumble flinched a little. “This is what happens when you get old,” he sighed, a wisp of smoke. “Everything gets a bit fuzzy.”

Lira, remembering her own worry about not being good enough, felt a pang. “Don’t worry, Puff. We’ll help you find them. We’re very good at finding things, aren’t we, Grumble?”

Grumble, who had a remarkable knack for hidden treasures, pointed. “There!” On the edge of a large dewy fern, glinting in a stray shaft of sun: magnificent, slightly smudged spectacles. Puff’s happy rumble vibrated the ground. He put them on, carefully. Eyes clear, twinkling.

“Wonderful! You’ve saved my eyesight. As a thank you, I can give you a ride anywhere. My wings are still quite strong.”

Lira’s eyes lit at flying. Then her heart leaped. The festival. The ribbon. Already late. So much time worrying and searching. “Could you take us to the Ferncrown festival grounds? As quickly as you can?”

Puff lowered his great head. “Climb aboard. Hold on tight.”

She hesitated. A quick ride meant even less time to finish, to make it truly perfect. Grumble nudged. “Come on, Lira. We promised to help Puff, and he’s helping us. It’s an adventure.” She saw the genuine kindness in Puff’s large clear eyes. The unexpected detour felt right. She hopped onto the broad mossy back. Grumble clambered behind.

A powerful graceful beat. Wind lifted her hair like a silken banner. The world below a colourful living tapestry. Forest sounds faded. Rush of air. Steady joyful wings. Pure wonder.

They landed with a gentle bump just as cheerful festival music began. Her ribbon: a tiny knot she hadn’t hidden, a slight unevenness in one petal. A familiar wave of worry. It wasn’t perfect.

Then she saw Puff watching, golden eyes warm. She remembered his rumbling sighs, and how they had offered help; Grumble, always ready. This ribbon, even with its tiny flaw, was more than a decoration. A shared journey. She offered it: silken threads cool, pearls like captured light, faint dried flowers.

Head high, she walked to the judging table. Dewdrop pearls caught the sun. The elf judge, wise twinkling eyes, kind smile.

“A unique piece. Such character and charm.” To her surprise, she was awarded a ribbon: not for perfect stitches or flawless symmetry, but for charming adventurous spirit. Not the most dazzling there. To Lira, the most special. Worry dissolved like morning mist. Puff waited at the edge of the crowd, spectacles straight. Grumble’s pockets still bulged. The knot in her work caught the light and did not apologise.
